title: Proof run
description: What one CI run of the test suites showed at one exact commit: an outcome for every automated test record in the spec, attested by the provider's trusted signer.
identity: The commit and the CI run

title: Gate verdict
description: Whether one commit passes a gate: the change gate against the base branch's head, or the release gate on its own.
identity: The commit and the gate kind

title: Module resolution
description: The modules one service needs, as go.mod and go.sum state them after STEGO resolved them from the captured source.

title: Module cache
description: The module zips that one source revision needs, downloaded once and recorded by digest, so every build of that revision can run with the network off.

title: Application build
description: One build of a service's executable from one source revision, with the record that names every input and the SBOMs written from it.

title: Application image
description: One container image of a built executable, with its record, its signature and where it was published.

title: Declaration
description: One service declaration, with everything it states: the archetype it selects, its entities and their fields, its collections, its slot bindings, its component settings and the modules its fills may import. All of it is written, reviewed and refused as one unit, so the declaration is the only root here. It holds eight entities, one more than the product's usual limit of seven, because it is one file; the limit was raised to 8 on 2026-10-28 for this reason.

title: Digest lifecycle
description: What happened to one component digest, or one runtime library version, after the registry published it: its supersession by a successor, and its withdrawal.
identity: The component name or the runtime library, and its digest or version
notes: Consistency boundary: a supersession and a withdrawal change the standing of one digest, and the rules between them concern that digest alone. A published digest never changes, and a consumer reads the registry through a pinned snapshot, so the lifecycle cannot live in the snapshot: a consumer on an old snapshot would never see it. Distributing owns this aggregate, not Supplying. Apply must refuse a pin past its date and a new pin to a withdrawn digest, and a specification can read only aggregates of its own domain. A policy that hears a Supplying event would also infer a successor, which ST-DIS-UC04-R02 forbids. The records are kept beside the registry and read from its current head, not from the pinned snapshot. A withdrawal is not an aggregate of its own, because it and the supersession of the same digest decide one standing together.

title: Compiler release
description: One compiler release at one exact source commit: the CI runs, required jobs and signed artifacts that qualify it, and the published assets that a consumer installs.
notes: Consistency boundary: qualification judges every run, job and artifact of one commit together, and verification checks the published release against that same qualification. A result from another commit belongs to another release. One signed compiler holds every generator (ST-STD-TRUST), so a release is the only unit that carries generator code. The compiler pin and the registry pin move apart: a release does not hold the registry.

title: Compiler installation
description: One compiler put in place on an operator's machine: the binary, its signed build record and the result folder that holds them.
notes: Consistency boundary: the installer checks every digest and both signatures, then puts the binary and its record in place together, or leaves nothing. It is not part of the release, because many installations come from one release, and an installation never changes the release.

title: Platform requirements
description: Everything one service needs its environment to supply, derived from service.yaml and the components it uses, with no environment values.

title: Delivery pipeline
description: The CI file STEGO writes for one service: a thin, pinned call to shared pipeline code, and the signer that pipeline's images must carry.

title: Kubernetes base
description: The plain kustomize base for one service: every Kubernetes resource derivable from service.yaml, and nothing that differs per environment.

title: Delivery object
description: The object a GitOps tool reads to deliver one service, written from the delivery stanza in service.yaml.

title: Delivery candidate
description: One image that a CI provider built, and the result of every STEGO check run on it before it may be released.
identity: The source revision and the image digest

title: Fill
description: One fill in a service's fills/ folder: hand-written code that implements one slot's contract for one collection, its tests, the evidence that the tests passed, and a person's signature of that evidence. It is written, tested and signed as one unit.

title: Service build
description: What one service's generated code was built from, together with that code: the record in .stego/state.yaml, the generated files it lists with their hashes, and the journal of an apply in progress.
notes: Consistency boundary: apply writes the generated files and the record as one journaled transaction, and recovery completes that same transaction. A file without its record, or a record without its files, is the failure this aggregate prevents. A component pin is not an aggregate of its own, because only apply changes it, together with the files it produced. Decision of 2026-10-27: the record extends .stego/state.yaml and does not live in a second file. It needs a service name, real per-component digests and a stated format contract. The format version exists today. The service name and the per-component digests do not.

title: Registry
description: The active registry: the archetypes, components and mixins that a service can be built from, composed from one common registry and the local registries that add to it, each pinned by one reference. A local registry may add to the common registry but may not replace a part of it. The components sit in this aggregate, because the rules on namespaces, replacement and stage hold across all of them at once.
identity: The content digest of the active registry

title: Archetype
description: A curated component set with its conventions: the golden path a service selects. It names the components it includes, the component that answers each port by default, and the mixins that extend it.

title: Port
description: A named contract between components: one component provides it and others require it. A port states the meaning of every field its providers fill, so two providers cannot mean different things by the same field.

title: Slot
description: A typed extension point a component declares, where a service binds its own rules. A slot that no generator invokes is dead, whatever binds to it.
identity: The slot name and its component
